newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end mixed as investors take profits.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end mixed as investors take profits.

text.p: Toronto stocks finished mixed due to profit taking on Tuesday, but not before Canada's biggest stock market touched an all-time high.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 27.41 points to close at 6305.46, off an intraday high of 6348.02 reached earlier in the day.
The key index posted its 12th record close of 1997 on Monday.
"We saw a bit of profit taking, but it's nothing to get worried about," said Ira Katzin, an investment advisor at RBC Dominion Securities.
Trading was brisk with 119.9 million shares changing hands worth C$2.1 billion ($1.5 billion).
Despite key index's decline, the overall market was mixed.
Advancing stocks outpaced declines 522 to 496 with 285 issues unchanged.
The financial services group surrendered 135 points, leading 10 of 14 sub-groups lower. Canadian bank stocks have recently powered the TSE's record gains..
Other weak sectors included consumer products, conglomerates and transportation. The TSE's strength was in precious metals, energy, utilities and retailing.
* Royal Bank of Canada topped active issues.
Royal Bank fell 1.40 to 60.65 on 4.3 million shares, but it reached a 52-week high of 63 earlier in the session.
Bank of Nova Scotia fell 1.90 to 55.20, while Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce dropped 1.45 to 69.45.
* Saskatchewan Wheat Pool class B was the biggest loser, sinking 2.30 to 16.50. The grain handling co-operative said on Tuesday it expected lower earnings due to shipping problems.
* Wascana Energy Inc. gained 0.15 to 19.10 on 1.9 million shares after the takeover target said it will consider Talisman Energy Inc's request to meet with its board.
Talisman has launched a C$1.7 billion ($1.2 billion) hostile bid for Wascana.
